!59 = !{!"/app/example.hlsl", !"//==========================================================================//\0A// What to look for: `Func` is an empty `inout` function -- its body never touches\0A// its parameter. `PSMain` pre-decrements `i` exactly once and passes that as\0A// Func's argument: `Func(--i)`. A correct compile therefore subtracts one input\0A// unit from the loaded value before storing it to the output. Compare the\0A// operand of the arithmetic instruction generated for the `--i` expression (near\0A// the DXIL disassembly's `StoreOutput`/`bufferStore` call) across the dxc panes:\0A// it currently subtracts two input units, not one -- the pre-decrement is\0A// applied twice. This does not depend on optimisation level or shader stage; it\0A// reproduces identically in the pixel-shader source tested locally and in the\0A// compute-shader restatement shown here.\0A//==========================================================================//\0A\0A// Compute-shader restatement of #4871's repro, for Compiler Explorer panes\0A// whose compilers cannot lower a pixel shader (e.g. hlsl_clang_trunk requires\0A// SV_Target to be a float type). The construct under test -- an empty inout\0A// function called with a pre-decremented argument -- is not stage-specific.\0ARWStructuredBuffer<uint> Out : register(u0);\0A\0Avoid Func(inout uint byteOffset)\0A{\0A}\0A\0A[numthreads(1, 1, 1)]\0Avoid CSMain(uint3 tid : SV_DispatchThreadID)\0A{\0A    uint i = tid.x;\0A    Func(--i);  // Subtracts 2...\0A    Out[0] = i;\0A}\0A"}
